About This Job
Netcompany is looking for data-focused professionals with at least two years’ experience supporting production database environments to join our team on a permanent basis. You will take ownership of your work and contribute to keeping database services secure, reliable and resilient, while developing your skills on complex client projects.
Key Responsibilities
• Support and maintain production databases, investigating incidents and resolving service issues.
• Monitor database health, availability and performance, identifying opportunities for improvement.
• Perform and validate database backups and restores, and support disaster recovery arrangements.
• Manage database access and implement changes through agreed security and change control processes.
• Maintain clear operational documentation and share knowledge with colleagues.
Essential
• At least two years’ experience supporting production systems, including hands-on experience with relational databases in an administration, development or operations role.
• An enthusiasm for data and a commitment to learning and developing new skills.
• A logical, proactive approach, with the ability to take ownership of work and recognise when to seek support.
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to a range of audiences and share knowledge with colleagues.
• Demonstrable problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, including identifying root causes and resolving database issues to maintain availability and efficient performance, supported by practical skills in query optimisation, index design and maintenance, and execution plan analysis.
• Demonstrable understanding of database schemas and design principles, including tables, relationships, keys, constraints and indexes.
• Demonstrable understanding of database high availability and disaster recovery approaches.
• Hands-on experience implementing database backup strategies, restoring databases and validating successful recovery, supported by a demonstrable understanding of recovery models.
• Familiarity with data migration approaches and tools, including extract, transform and load (ETL) processes.
• Demonstrable understanding of database access controls and the principle of least privilege.
• Ability to write and maintain reliable SQL and administrative scripts, and apply production changes safely through impact assessment, testing and rollback planning.
• Experience using monitoring tools to assess database health, availability and performance, investigate alerts and take appropriate action.
• Eligibility to obtain the security clearance required for the role.

Qualifications
Desirable
• Experience testing database code or administrative scripts, including unit testing where appropriate.
• Understanding of ITIL fundamentals, particularly incident, problem and change management.
• Experience working with cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure or AWS.
• Experience supporting wider IT infrastructure.

Additional Information
Netcompany Academy
Through our Netcompany Academy, we offer a diverse range of courses, seminars and certifications carefully curated to support your development. As you advance in your career, the Academy tailors its offerings to enhance your managerial skills, deepen your understanding of methodologies, hone your leadership abilities, and fine-tune your strategic acumen.
As you progress through the content, you’ll naturally take on more responsibility and network with your peers.
Benefits include
• 25 days’ holiday
• Private Medical Health care via Vitality
• Pension contribution, Life Assurance
• Professional certifications supported as part of learning and development.
• A range of retail discounts to enhance your lifestyle, encompassing restaurants, supermarkets, travel, leisure activities and health and well-being services.
• Access to our Employee Resource Groups, our groups represent diverse backgrounds and provide a platform for colleagues to connect, learn, and support one another.
Company information
At Netcompany, we pride ourselves on our entrepreneurial spirit and our capacity for doing things differently. Our culture is built on fostering low bureaucracy, emphasizing high agility and promoting flexibility, enabling everyone to contribute their best.
Our journey began in the UK with the acquisition of Hunter Macdonald in 2017. As one of Northern Europe's most accomplished IT companies, we have expanded our headcount globally to 7400+ employees and have offices in UK, Denmark, Norway, Poland, Holland and Vietnam.
Netcompany is committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free recruitment process for anyone wishing to apply for a job with us. We operate a Disability Confident Interview Scheme which means that we offer guaranteed interviews to all applicants with a disability who meet the minimum criteria for a role. Applicants are asked to opt in, so please let us know if you wish your application to be considered under this scheme.
If you need any reasonable adjustments or extra support during the recruitment process, please contact us at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com.

About This Job
Are you an experienced Control & Instrumentation Engineer looking to work on some of the most advanced and complex engineering challenges in the UK?
The salary for this role is £64,820 (inclusive of a Specialist Allowance).
This role is based at the following site: Culham, Oxfordshire
The Role
The Control & Instrumentation Group provides organisation-wide expertise, support and services for UKAEA projects, with strong capability in the design, delivery, installation and commissioning of electrical, control and instrumentation systems. Our work underpins major operational facilities today while helping shape future fusion technologies.
As Senior Control & Instrumentation Engineer, you will provide and apply key technical skills related to Control and Instrumentation systems to enable the successful delivery of projects and programmes across UKAEA.
The role holder will act as a subject matter expert in control and instrumentation, leading and owning large, high-risk work packages involving complex systems and technical studies.
Key Accountabilities:
•
Lead medium-to-large scale fusion C&I projects from concept through to detailed design for facility upgrades and future technologies.
•
Act as Subject Matter Expert for control and instrumentation systems across projects and programmes.
•
Produce or contribute to technical decision papers, involving innovative problem solving of novel situations, analysing unprecedent technical issues and influencing strategic project direction and approaches.
•
Develop control system architectures and solutions, specifications, and documentation, applying innovative solutions to complex technical challenges.
•
Provide technical leadership for control and safety systems, covering architecture design, software development, installation, commissioning, and lifecycle management.
•
Lead and deliver software development using industrial control platforms (e.g. Siemens S7/PCS7, LabVIEW, ABB 800xA, Python, C++).
• Manage project delivery, including requirements capture, design reviews, HAZOPs, risk management, budgets, and stakeholder engagement.
• Coordinate and mentor multidisciplinary teams and contractors, ensuring safe, high-quality, and cost-effective delivery in line with organisational and regulatory standards.
This role is primarily onsite due to the nature of the work and the facilities involved. However, hybrid working can be discussed where possible, depending on business needs.

Qualifications
Essential:
•
A degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or equivalent, and relevant professional experience in an engineering role. Or a minimum of a HND in Electrical/Electronic discipline, or equivalent qualification level, with a greater breadth and depth of experience/knowledge.
•
Excellent knowledge and significant experience of PLC and SCADA systems
• Demonstrable experience with Siemens, ABB 800Xa or similar control system applications.
• Deep understanding of EC&I documents (SLDs, P&IDs, C&Es, schematics etc.)
• Advanced knowledge and understanding of safe working practices and procedures, with substantial experience of preparing safety documentation (i.e. risk assessments, method statements, permits, isolations etc).
•
Demonstrable experience in design, installation and testing of Control and Instrumentation software and hardware systems.
•
Identify policy/process improvements in C&I engineering and contribute to proposals that influence organisational standards and governance.
• Experience working in a scientific / engineering environment following strict safety processes, collaborating with a broad variety of stakeholders
This role requires employees to complete an online Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), including The Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS) checks for criminal convictions and possibly a search of open source data.

Additional Information
A full list of our benefits can be found here https://careers.ukaea.uk/life-at-ukaea/employee-benefits/

About This Job
Lead Data Scientist - Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Handling & Prevent
We’re looking for a Lead Data Scientist (IC3) to join our Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Handling & Prevent team in London.
This role is a unique opportunity to work on the AI and intelligence systems at the core of our operational handling and prevention work. You'll help build and automate components of our operational systems using Generative AI, LLMs and agentic AI approaches, establish robust LLM evaluation pipelines, and build solutions that reduce financial crime risk. What you build will have a direct impact on Wise’s mission and millions of our customers.
The AML Handling & Prevent team offers an exciting environment for applying cutting-edge Generative AI, Agentic AI and machine learning architectures. This team is dedicated to enhancing our financial crime mitigation operations through advanced tooling, automated evaluation frameworks, prompt optimisation and increasingly autonomous AI workflows, aiming to streamline reviews and simplify the work of our operations staff. As a Lead Data Scientist (IC3), you will drive technical strategy across handling and prevent initiatives, architect robust AI systems, establish post-deployment monitoring, and lead complex automation initiatives to reduce financial crime risk across Wise.
Here’s how you’ll be contributing:
•
End-to-End AI Automation & EDD LLMs: Lead the development and deployment of AI models designed to augment operational workflows (e.g. Business and Consumer EDD LLMs), specifically targeting the automation of case summaries, red flag generation, risk classifications, document requests and agentic workflows.
•
Evaluation Framework & Labeling Taxonomy: Establish labeling taxonomies and guidelines with EDD SMEs, construct evaluation datasets, and implement automated eval harnesses to systematically measure accuracy, precision, recall, and failure modes.
•
Prompt Optimization & Experimentation: Audit existing prompts and run structured experiments (few-shot, chain-of-thought, context ordering) within a hypothesis-driven testing framework to reduce hallucinations, formatting errors, and prompt drift.
•
Agentic AI Systems: Help design and develop AI workflows that can reason across multiple steps, use tools and contextual information, and support complex operational processes safely and reliably.
•
Shadow Testing & Monitoring: Design shadow mode deployments and parallel execution testing to safely evaluate prompts and AI workflows at scale, while implementing post-deployment monitoring for data and output drift.
•
Full-Stack Deployment: Take ownership of the production pipeline by writing and deploying production-ready Python services. You must be willing to bypass engineering bottlenecks to ship value quickly while maintaining code quality.
•
Human-in-the-Loop Architecture: Design systems where AI provides recommendations and drafts, ensuring human operators retain the final decision-making authority for critical financial crime mitigation assessments.
•
Strategic Demand Deflection: Go beyond ticket handling by analyzing upstream data to create strategies that deflect financial crime attempts before they reach the operations team, effectively reducing manual workload.
•
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Set technical direction, mentor Senior and Junior Data Scientists, foster a product-focused mindset, and guide the team through complex technical implementations, architectural decisions, and AI governance standards.

•
Experience implementing, training, testing and evaluating performance of Machine Learning systems;
•
Strong Python knowledge. A big plus for proven familiarity and experience with OOP principles;
•
Some hands-on experience developing or working with GenAI / LLM solutions. You don’t need to be an LLM specialist, but you should have professional exposure to areas such as prompt engineering, evaluation, LLM-powered workflows or Agentic AI;
•
Knowledge and experience developing and evaluating GenAI / LLM solutions, including automated eval harnesses and prompt engineering;
•
Experience with statistical analysis, experiment design, and failure mode analysis in ML or LLM systems;
•
A strong product mindset with the ability to work independently in a cross-functional and cross-team environment;
•
Good communication skills and ability to get the point across to non-technical individuals and SMEs;

Strong problem solving skills with the ability to help refine problem statements and figure out how to solve them.

Familiarity with automating operational processes via technical solutions, for example Large Language Models, AI agents or multi-step AI workflows

About This Job
The Regulatory Reporting Accountant is responsible for the timely and accurate preparation of regulatory returns to the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and Bank of England (BoE). The role plays a key part in ensuring regulatory compliance through the production of COREP, FINREP and other prudential and statistical returns.
The role will also support the ongoing enhancement of the regulatory reporting framework through automation, process improvement and data quality initiatives. Working closely with Finance, Risk, Treasury, Technology and other stakeholders across the Bank, the role will ensure reporting processes remain robust, efficient and aligned with evolving regulatory requirements.
Key Responsibilities:
• Preparation of regulatory statistical and supervisory returns to the Bank of England / Prudential Regulation Authority / Financial Conduct Authority / European Banking Authority, including Common Reporting.
• Review and analysis of the returns to ensure timely and accurate production of the reports in line with reporting definitions.
• Assist with implementation and automation of current and forthcoming regulatory returns.
• Assist with improving data extract in line with the regulatory definitions.
• Assist with designing reports to extract information to support regulatory returns.
• Liaising with team members within Finance and other stakeholders within the bank with the view to enhance data quality.
• Maintain and update regulatory reporting documentation, policies and procedures.
• Assist with any other external reporting if required.
• Support the production of other external reporting requirements as and when required.

Qualifications
Skills & Experience:
• Experience in regulatory reporting within a banking or financial services environment.
• Good understanding of prudential regulatory frameworks and reporting requirements, including COREP, FINREP and statistical reporting.
• Up-to-date knowledge of PRA, FCA and BoE regulatory developments and policy requirements.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
• Advanced Excel skills and experience using regulatory reporting systems and data extraction tools.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple functions.
• Ability to work under pressure and manage competing priorities to meet tight regulatory deadlines.
• Proactive approach to process improvement, automation and enhancing control frameworks.
• Highly organised with strong planning and prioritisation skills.
• Team-oriented approach with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organisation.
• Demonstrates Shawbrook values through openness, transparency, accountability, and a commitment to excellence.
• Ability to use regulatory reporting software such as Suade, Regnology or similar.
• Accounting / Professional Qualifications
Education / Professional Qualifications
Shawbrook is committed to providing opportunities to all candidates and understands that not all candidates may possess qualifications directly aligned to the role. We will assess each candidate on their individual experience, skills, and potential, and not solely on educational qualifications.
Preferred:
• An accounting qualification.
• Relevant experience in UK banking regulatory reporting.
• Experience with regulatory reporting platforms and reporting automation initiatives.

Additional Information

• Market leading family friendly policies such as access to our Maternity, Adoption and Paternity policies from Day 1 of your employment

• Free access to Peppy digital health app that offers personalised support through fertility treatment becoming a parent or menopause
• EAP (Employee Assistance Programme) - Offering you support on a wide range of subjects including financial concerns, mental wellbeing and more general queries around family, work, housing and health

• Discounts on gym membership
• Contributory pension scheme & death in service
Your Lifestyle - It’s important you strike the right balance between your work and personal life. We provide benefits to support you when at work and when you’re enjoying your leisure time.

• Option to buy or sell holiday days through our flexi-holiday scheme

• Access to discounts on a range of high street and online brands

About This Job
Associate Structural Engineer – Bristol
We invite you to bring your talent and passion into play as an Associate Structural Engineer in our growing Bristol team.
This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced structural engineer who wants to combine technical leadership, project delivery, client relationships and business growth. You’ll play an important role in our Industry & Infrastructure Facilities (I&IF) team, helping us deliver technically interesting projects while also helping shape and grow our presence in Bristol.
If you are looking for a role where you can remain close to engineering, work with great people and have a genuine influence on the direction of a growing team, we’d love to hear from you.
A great place to build your career
You’ll join our Industry & Infrastructure Facilities (I&IF) team in Bristol – a growing regional team with a real sense of community and a strong focus on technical excellence.
Our work spans a diverse range of sectors, including rail, aviation, energy, manufacturing, data centres and other critical infrastructure. The variety of our work means you’ll have the opportunity to apply your structural engineering expertise to different challenges, clients and sectors.
We work across the project lifecycle, from early feasibility and concept development through to detailed design and construction. We also work closely with colleagues across Ramboll, bringing together structural, civil, MEP, sustainability and other specialist expertise to deliver integrated solutions.
Why Bristol?
We’re a smaller regional team, which means you’ll have the opportunity to make a real contribution and see the impact of your work. There is a strong sense of community, with technically excellent people around you who are keen to share knowledge, support each other and help you develop.
We also like to have some fun. Our active Bristol social team organises activities ranging from padel and other sports to pub quizzes and informal team events.
Our Bristol office is in a great location, close to Temple Meads and Bristol city centre, providing a collaborative and accessible base for our growing team.
Your role
Your role As an Associate Structural Engineer, you will have a broad role combining technical, project, people and business responsibilities.
You will:
• Lead the structural design and delivery of technically complex or specialised projects, taking responsibility for technical quality and project outcomes.
• Develop structural concepts, design philosophies and innovative engineering solutions.
• Act as a technical point of reference for colleagues, sharing your knowledge and providing coaching and guidance to other engineers.
• Take responsibility for client relationships and represent Ramboll at project and technical meetings.
• Work closely with architects, contractors and other disciplines to develop practical, coordinated and efficient solutions.
• Promote sustainable and low-carbon approaches to structural design, including reuse and efficient use of materials.
• Support the development of the Bristol I&IF team and contribute to building our technical capability.
• Identify opportunities to improve the way we deliver our work and develop new services and areas of expertise.
Help shape our Bristol growth
A key part of this role will be helping to develop and deliver the Bristol I&IF growth strategy.
Working closely with the Bristol I&IF leadership team and our Growth & Business Development colleagues, you will:
• Help identify sectors, clients and opportunities where Ramboll’s expertise can add value.
• Contribute to the development of our local market and client strategy.
• Build and maintain relationships with existing and prospective clients.
• Help develop and pursue opportunities, from early conversations through to bids and appointments.
• Work with colleagues across Ramboll to identify opportunities to bring together our wider multidisciplinary expertise.
• Play a key role in turning the Bristol I&IF growth strategy into action and helping to build a sustainable pipeline of work.
We are looking for someone who is curious about clients and their challenges, enjoys building relationships and wants to play an active role in shaping the future of the team.
What we’re looking for
For this role, we believe your starting point is:
• Chartered with the IStructE, ICE or an international equivalent.
• Significant experience as a structural engineer, with a strong track record of delivering technically challenging projects.
• A high level of technical competence and sound engineering judgement across steel, concrete and/or timber.
• Experience taking technical responsibility for projects and providing guidance to other engineers.
• The ability to work independently on complex or specialised engineering problems, with limited oversight.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex engineering principles clearly to clients, colleagues and other stakeholders.
• The ability to develop strong and lasting relationships with clients and collaborators.
• A collaborative approach and a willingness to coach and support others.
• A commercial mindset and an interest in understanding clients’ needs and identifying opportunities.
• A passion for finding better, more efficient and more sustainable ways of solving engineering problems.
Experience in rail, aviation, energy, manufacturing, data centres or other critical infrastructure is essential, but we don’t expect you to have experience across all of these areas. We are interested in strong engineers who are excited by the opportunity to apply their skills to new and varied challenges.
Your opportunity to make a difference
This is an opportunity to join a team that is growing and have a genuine influence on what it becomes.
You’ll have the support of experienced technical specialists across Bristol, the wider UK I&IF team and Ramboll’s international network, while having the autonomy to lead projects, develop client relationships, support colleagues and contribute to the growth strategy for the Bristol business.
If you’re looking for an Associate role where you can combine great engineering with leadership, client relationships and business growth – while remaining part of a close-knit regional team – we’d love to hear from you.
Ready to join us?
Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your CV.
We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.
Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.
Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll
Ramboll is a global architect

We are seeking an experienced and commercially focused Director of Treasury to lead the UK Occupier Client Treasury function supporting the Colliers Global Occupier Services platform.
This is a strategic leadership role responsible for the governance, performance and continuous improvement of client treasury operations across a significant portfolio of occupier accounts. The role will ensure the effective management of client funds, banking structures, cash forecasting, payment operations, controls, compliance and treasury risk management on behalf of our clients.
Working closely with Head of Treasury Service and Global Occupier Services leadership, account teams, finance leaders and key client stakeholders, the Director of Treasury will provide strategic direction, operational oversight and treasury expertise while ensuring best-in-class service delivery, regulatory compliance and risk management.
The successful candidate will play a critical role in supporting the growth of the Occupier Services business, enhancing treasury capabilities and reinforcing our reputation as a trusted advisor to some of the world's leading corporate occupiers.
Key Responsibilities
Treasury Leadership & Strategy
•
Lead the development of the UK Occupier Client Treasury function, ensuring alignment with Global Occupier Services objectives and client requirements.
•
Define and implement the strategic roadmap for treasury operations, controls, technology and service delivery.
•
Provide leadership and guidance to treasury managers and specialists, fostering a high-performance and client-focused culture.
•
Partner with UK and Global leadership teams to support business growth, client retention and new client onboarding.
•
Act as the senior treasury advisor for occupier clients and internal stakeholders.
Client Funds Management
•
Oversee the management of client monies held across a wide range of occupier accounts.
•
Ensure all client funds are managed in accordance with contractual obligations, regulatory requirements and best practice.
•
Maintain robust controls over bank account structures, authorisations and cash movements.
•
Monitor liquidity requirements across client portfolios and ensure operational funding obligations are met.
•
Drive optimisation of cash management processes while maintaining strong governance standards.
Treasury Operations & Payments
•
Provide oversight of high-volume payment and receivables operations supporting occupier clients.
•
Ensure efficient and controlled processing of supplier payments, landlord payments, tax obligations and other disbursements.
•
Establish and monitor Treasury Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and operational performance metrics.
•
Lead operational resilience planning for treasury processes and banking infrastructure.
•
Ensure treasury operations support evolving client and business requirements.
Banking & Relationship Management
•
Manage relationships with banking partners supporting UK Client Treasury activities.
•
Lead the establishment, rationalisation and governance of client bank account structures.
•
Support banking due diligence and onboarding requirements for new client mandates.
•
Oversee banking service reviews, fee analysis and service optimisation initiatives.
•
Collaborate with global treasury counterparts on strategic banking initiatives and technology solutions.
Cash Forecasting & Liquidity Management
•
Develop and enhance short, medium and long-term client cash forecasting capabilities.
•
Ensure appropriate liquidity management practices are in place across client portfolios.
•
Provide actionable insights to account leadership teams regarding cash positions and funding requirements.
•
Improve forecasting accuracy through reporting automation and enhanced data analytics.
•
Support strategic decision-making through comprehensive treasury reporting and analysis.
Treasury Risk Management
•
Identify, assess and manage treasury-related risks across client operations, including:
•
Liquidity risk
•
Operational risk
•
Counterparty and banking risk
•
Payment fraud and cyber risk
•
Regulatory and compliance risk
•
Ensure robust segregation of duties and treasury control frameworks are maintained.
•
Lead treasury governance reviews and control enhancement programmes.
•
Support enterprise risk management initiatives relevant to client treasury activities.
Governance, Compliance & Controls
•
Ensure treasury activities comply with all client contractual obligations, internal policies and regulatory requirements.
•
Maintain strong governance frameworks for client money management and treasury operations.
•
Support internal and external audits relating to treasury activities.
•
Ensure treasury policies, procedures and control documentation remain current and fit for purpose.
•
Deliver executive-level reporting on treasury performance, risk and compliance matters.
Stakeholder & Client Management
•
Build trusted relationships with senior client contacts and act as an ambassador for the Treasury function.
•
Partner with Account Directors, Client Finance teams, Lease Administration, Facilities Management and Procurement teams.
•
Provide treasury expertise during client bids, transitions and account expansions.
•
Present treasury strategies, performance updates and risk assessments to senior stakeholders.
•
Collaborate closely with Global Occupier Services and Corporate Finance leadership teams.
Technology & Transformation
•
Drive treasury transformation initiatives across systems, controls and reporting platforms.
•
Identify opportunities for automation, digitisation and process simplification.
•
Lead treasury-related system implementations and enhancements.
•
Leverage data analytics and technology to improve visibility, accuracy and control.
•
Champion continuous improvement and innovation across the Client Treasury function.
About You
You are a highly credible treasury leader with extensive experience managing complex treasury operations in a client-focused environment.
You combine strong technical treasury knowledge with exceptional leadership and stakeholder management skills. You are comfortable operating at both a strategic and operational level and have a proven track record of building high-performing teams while delivering excellent client outcomes.
You thrive in a fast-paced professional services environment and enjoy solving complex problems, influencing stakeholders and driving operational excellence.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential
•
Significant treasury leadership experience within corporate real estate, outsourcing, professional services, banking or a related industry.
•
Extensive experience managing client funds, treasury operations and cash management activities.
•
Proven experience leading treasury teams and developing talent.
•
Strong understanding of treasury controls, governance frameworks and operational risk management.

About This Job
About the Role
We are looking for an Senior FP&A Analyst to join the IFS Copperleaf finance team, based in the UK. You will be one of five in a close-knit, high-calibre FP&A team, working together on the forecast, planning and reporting cycle while owning your own areas of forecasting, performance reporting and commercial analysis.
The rest of the team is based in Vancouver, so this role carries the European day. You will be the FP&A point of contact for stakeholders across the UK and Europe, working autonomously while your colleagues are offline and handing over cleanly across time zones. As one of the senior members of the team, you will be someone we can look to when the Director, FP&A is not in the room.
The value of this role is not in producing the numbers, it is in explaining them. We need someone with real commercial awareness who can see the bigger picture, get to the insight behind the movement and put a clear recommendation in front of decision-makers. You will act as a trusted finance business partner, working cross-functionally with leaders across the business, and will mentor and develop junior members of the FP&A team.
This is also a data-forward role. Copperleaf is a fast-paced, high-growth business and we expect this role to be fluent with data - comfortable querying source systems directly, building production reporting in the Power Platform, and using AI and agentic workflows to shorten the distance between question and answer. We want someone with the tenacity to keep finding improvements in efficiency, quality and capability, and the toolset and appetite to build them rather than wait for them.
Key Responsibilities
Commercial Insight and Business Partnering
• Act as a trusted finance business partner to leaders across the business - understand their drivers, challenge assumptions and hold the business to its numbers.
• Explain performance rather than report it: connect movements in revenue, cost, headcount and KPIs to what is actually happening commercially, and set out what it means.
• Provide the analysis behind investment cases, pricing decisions and strategic initiatives, with a clear recommendation attached.
• Be the FP&A presence through the European day - the point of contact for UK and European stakeholders while the Vancouver-based team is offline.
• Be a senior voice in the team - sharpening the work of others, representing FP&A with senior stakeholders and picking things up when the Director, FP&A is unavailable.
Forecasting and Planning
• Play a leading role in the monthly and quarterly forecast cycle - owning your inputs, assumptions and commentary, and working with the team to land the submission.
• Build and maintain the models that underpin the plan: recurring revenue and backlog, ARR and ACV, churn and retention, cost, headcount and long-range planning.
• Support the annual planning process, bringing a clear view of where the risks and opportunities sit.
Reporting and Analysis
• Own the management reporting and dashboards that leaders use to run the business, with a narrative attached to every pack.
• Analyse variances, trends, risks and opportunities across revenue, operating expenses, headcount and KPIs.
• Partner with Accounting to ensure results are reported accurately and consistently.
Data, Automation and AI
• Get to the data at source - write and maintain queries against finance and operational data sets rather than waiting on manual extracts.
• Build and maintain automated reporting across the Microsoft Power Platform (Power Query, Power BI, Power Automate).
• Design and build agentic workflows that remove manual effort from the reporting and forecast cycle and increase our speed to insight.
• Use AI routinely in day-to-day analysis and raise the data and AI capability of the wider FP&A team.
• Bring a continuous improvement mindset - actively look for opportunities to improve efficiency, quality and capability, and see them through to delivery.

Qualifications
Essential
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field, or a qualified / part-qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA).
• 4-6 years of progressive FP&A, financial analysis or strategic finance experience.
• Strong commercial acumen, with a track record of influencing decisions rather than only producing analysis.
• Advanced Excel and financial modelling, with a solid grounding in accounting principles and the financial statements.
• Demonstrable experience working with large data sets and advanced data querying - SQL, Power Query / M or equivalent. You should be comfortable getting to the data yourself.
• Hands-on experience with the Microsoft Power Platform (Power BI, Power Query, Power Automate), building and maintaining reporting rather than only consuming it.
• Practical experience embedding AI into finance workflows, with concrete examples of what you built, what it replaced and what it delivered.
• Able to tell the story behind the numbers and influence credibly at senior level.
• Thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with the tenacity to drive continuous improvement.
• Comfortable working autonomously in a distributed, cross-time-zone team, with the judgement to make decisions and progress work without waiting for the wider team to come online.
Desirable
• Experience as a senior or lead analyst, including mentoring others or standing in for a finance lead.
• Experience building AI agents or agentic workflows (for example Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Claude, or Python-based agents).
• Experience with Workday Adaptive Planning or a comparable EPM / planning tool.
• Python or similar scripting for data manipulation.
• SaaS or technology sector experience, including exposure to recurring revenue metrics (ARR, ACV, churn, backlog) and project / services revenue recognition.

Additional Information
What We’re Offering
• Salary Range: £70,000 annually + bonus
• Flexible paid time off, including sick and holiday
• Medical, dental, & vision insurance
• Flexible spending accounts
• Life insurance and disability benefits
• Tuition assistance
• Community involvement and volunteering events
Additional Information
We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

Your customers are the developers, security teams, and operational teams at our partners. Companies like Morgan Stanley, N26 and Ramp rely on Wise Platform APIs to run critical payments journeys in production. It’s your job to ensure they can connect securely, operate reliably, and troubleshoot issues quickly — without needing manual support.

Design in partnership with the Security team, credential management, authentication strategies, and secure connection protocols that balance security with developer experience.
•
Build and improve webhook reliability, observability, and usability.
•
Deliver API and webhook logs and diagnostics tooling that helps partners and internal teams investigate and recover from issues faster.
•
Ensure the auth and security infrastructure of Wise Platform is robust and scalable for the long term service demands.

Own the roadmap
•
Define and execute a roadmap centred on secure access, reliability, and operational excellence in production.
Drive execution

Work closely with engineering to ship improvements that measurably reduce incidents, support load, and time-to-resolution.

Make pragmatic trade-offs between scope, security, reliability, and delivery speed.

About This Job
At ASOS, we're building the next generation of AI-powered Search and Discovery experiences for millions of customers worldwide.
Our Search & Recommendations team develops the platforms, infrastructure and machine learning systems that power personalised product discovery, ranking, retrieval and recommendation experiences across ASOS. We operate high-scale production systems that enable data scientists and ML engineers to rapidly develop, deploy and monitor machine learning solutions in a reliable, scalable and cost-effective way.
We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer - with strong Engineering experience - who enjoys solving complex engineering challenges at scale. This role is ideal for someone with a strong software engineering/MLOps, distributed systems or platform engineering background who wants to work at the intersection of machine learning and production infrastructure.
As a Senior Engineer, you'll be responsible for designing, building and operating the platforms and services that enable machine learning models to be trained, deployed and served reliably across ASOS.
You'll work closely with Applied Scientists, Software Engineers, Data Engineers and Product Managers to create the tooling, infrastructure and deployment frameworks that power recommendation systems, search relevance, personalisation and emerging AI applications.
This is a highly engineering-focused role with an emphasis on cloud-native systems, platform architecture, automation, observability and operational excellence.
What You'll Be Doing:
• Design and build scalable machine learning platforms and infrastructure supporting model training, deployment and serving.
• Develop highly available backend services that power recommendation, search and personalisation experiences for millions of customers.
• Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for machine learning and data products.
• Design batch and real-time inference architectures using modern cloud-native technologies.
• Improve reliability, resilience and performance across ML workloads through monitoring, observability and automation.
• Build tooling and frameworks that enable data scientists and ML engineers to deploy models safely and efficiently.
• Own production services, infrastructure and operational excellence practices, including incident management and root cause analysis.
• Optimise distributed compute workloads and resource utilisation across cloud environments.
• Drive Infrastructure-as-Code adoption and platform standardisation across machine learning systems.
• Contribute to architectural decisions across recommendation, search and AI platforms.
• Mentor engineers and promote software engineering best practices across the organisation.
• Help shape ASOS's long-term machine learning platform strategy.

Qualifications
We're interested in candidates who bring experience across modern software engineering, distributed systems and machine learning infrastructure. We recognise that expertise can be developed through a variety of backgrounds, including Backend Engineering, Platform Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Cloud Engineering, MLOps or Machine Learning Engineering.
We'd love to see experience in several of the following:
• Strong software engineering fundamentals with experience designing and building production systems at scale.
• Experience developing distributed systems, microservices or high-throughput backend platforms.
• Strong programming skills in Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, Scala or similar languages.
• Experience building and operating services in AWS, Azure or GCP environments.
• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, containerisation and cloud-native technologies.
• Experience implementing CI/CD pipelines and automated deployment processes.
• Knowledge of Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform, Pulumi or CloudFormation.
• Experience with monitoring, alerting and observability tooling.
• Experience building reliable, resilient and scalable systems with a focus on performance and operational excellence.
• Experience working with data-intensive systems, streaming technologies or large-scale distributed processing platforms.
• Exposure to machine learning systems, model serving, feature stores, training infrastructure or MLOps practices.
• Experience supporting recommendation systems, search platforms, personalisation engines or other customer-facing data products is advantageous.
• Comfortable providing technical leadership, mentoring engineers and influencing architectural direction.
• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience working in cross-functional product teams.
• Experience supporting large-scale model training and inference workloads.
• Knowledge of vector search, ranking systems, retrieval architectures or recommendation platforms.
• Exposure to LLMs, Generative AI and production AI systems.
• Experience building internal developer platforms, engineering enablement tooling or shared capabilities used across multiple teams.

Additional Information
BeneFITS’
• Employee discount (hello ASOS discount!)
• Employee sample sales
• 25 days paid annual leave + an extra celebration day for a special moment
• Discretionary bonus scheme
• Private medical care scheme
• Flexible benefits allowance - which you can choose to take as extra cash, or use towards other benefits
• Opportunity for personalised learning and in-the-moment experiences that enable you to thrive and excel in your role

About This Job
Job Purpose / Overview
The Pressure Compliance Mechanical Engineer will report to the Pressure System Completions and Integration Manager and will take responsibility for managing the pressure systems compliance and structural integrity requirements on behalf of a specific scope identified by the Pressure System Completions and Integration Manager and Pressure Compliance Lead, ensuring appropriate implementation and compliance to meet HPC project needs.
The role holder will support the implementation of pressure systems compliance and structural integrity requirements within specific projects, on behalf of a specific programme. They will support the project managers in ensuring compliance and delivery for HPC.
The role will require good technical and organisational capabilities to effectively interface with Project Managers and relevant stakeholders in the programme, the ONR, third party organisations and support the supply chain in delivery.
Their team and role will act as the single point of contact for pressure systems compliance and structural integrity requirements – through all phases of the project and for the various project policies, for their allocated scope.
The role may require trips abroad (mostly mainland Europe).
Contextual Information
Hinkley Point C is one of the largest power generation projects in the world, and the first nuclear station for a generation to be built in the UK.

About This Job
We are looking for a talented Network Engineer to join our growing global team at Sectigo.
The Network Engineer is responsible for supporting, implementing, managing, and maintaining the organization's networking infrastructure. This individual is detail-oriented, thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, and possesses a proven track record in learning, implementing, and maintaining enterprise networks and new technologies. Must be a commutable distance to Manchester DC, should the need arise.
Here are the core functions, responsibilities, and expectations for this role:
• Network: Designing, planning, and implementing network infrastructure move, add, or changes. Including maintenance and support.
• Network Security: Implementing and maintaining network security protocols, including firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS), VPNs, access control lists (ACLs), and encryption technologies to safeguard the organization's data and systems.
• Network Troubleshooting and Optimization: Diagnosing and resolving complex network issues, analyzing network performance, and optimizing network infrastructure to ensure high availability, reliability, and performance.
• Documentation and Reporting: Creating and maintaining network documentation, diagrams, and standard operating procedures (SOPs). Generating reports on network performance, security incidents, and compliance status for management review.
• Capacity Planning: Assessing current and future network capacity requirements based on business growth projections and technology trends. Planning and implementing scalability solutions to accommodate increasing demand.
• Regulatory Compliance: Ensuring network infrastructure compliance with industry regulations, standards, and best practices (e.g., PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO, Webtrust). Conducting audits and implementing remediation measures as needed.
• Mounting and Installation: Ability to mount and install network devices such as routers, switches, and servers in data centers and office locations. This includes rack mounting, cable management, and hardware configuration. Candidates must be able to lift network equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
• Travel & Operational Requirements:
• Participate in on-call rotation.
• Travel both internationally and nationally as needed (site support meetings, projects, etc.).
• Frequent visits to Datacenter near Manchester.
• Additional tasks associated with this position may be assigned in response to company initiatives and business needs.
More information about this role:
• This is a full-time and remote position based in U.K., with the ideal candidate reside within 1-hour driving distance to the greater Manchester area.
• The targeted compensation package for this role is between GBP 55,000 and 62,000 per annum, subject upon internal equity and years of experience.  We may make further adjustments through an approval process if the targeted compensation range needs to be modified based on business needs and market trends.

Qualifications
Education:
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, or related field is strongly preferred.  Relevant certifications (e.g., CCNP, CCIE, CISSP) are a plus.
Experience:
• Proven experience (typically 5+ years) in network engineering roles, with a focus on supporting, implementing, and managing enterprise-scale network infrastructures.
• Automation and Infrastructure as Code (IAC):
• Ability to create, implement, and maintain automation using Terraform and Ansible.
• Proficiency with GIT.
• Comfortable with JSON, YAML, and XML.
• Knowledge of Python is a plus.
• Cloud Environments:
• AWS network experience is necessary (TGWs, Network ACLs, AWS Network Firewall, Security Groups, VPCs, Subnet,etc..), and general experience is required.
• Must be proficient in installing, implementing, supporting, and maintaining Juniper, Palo Alto, and Arista hardware and software for Datacenter and Campus environments.
• Knowledge of SD-WAN technologies such as Palo Alto, Aruba/Silverpeak, or Cisco/Viptela is a plus.
• Site to Site VPN: Must be able to design, implement, and support Route based and Policy based VPN. Knowledge of specific technologies such as DMVPN, FlexVPN, and other vendor-specific VPNs is a plus.
• RA VPN: Must be able to design, implement, and support enterprise VPNs such as Global Protect or AnyConnect.
• VXLAN: Understanding of overlay vs underlay and how it interacts with EVPN
• AAA: Must be able to support, implement, and maintain Radius and Tacacs+ for both device access management and NAC (e.g., 802.1x). SAML-based authentication is a plus.
• Network Monitoring: Must be able to implement, support, and use: Netflow, SNMP, and related enterprise tools (e.g., Solarwinds, Nagios, LiveNX).
• FW Technologies and Traffic Flow: Must understand stateful vs non-stateful rules, symmetric vs non-symmetric, NAT types, order of operation, etc.
• L3 Routing Protocols: Must have knowledge of OSPFv2, OSPFv3 and BGP. Knowledge of others such as ISIS and mBGP is a plus.
• L3: Must know IPv6. IPv4 and IPv6 dual stack is a plus.
• Layer 2: Must understand rSTP, dot1q, vlan, L2 security
• Wireless: Good understanding wireless, roaming, troubleshooting
• HA: Must understand FHRP (VRRP, HSRP, etc.), LACP, BFD, switch stacks.etc.
• TCP/IP: Must understand path MTU discovery (ICMP), basic TCP flags, etc.
• DNS, DHCP, ARP, Neighbor Discovery: Must have a good understanding.
• Segment Packet Frame troubleshooting: Must be comfortable packet captures and utilizing tools like Wireshark and tcpdump.
Ideal Candidate Profiles, Talents, and Desired Qualifications:
• In-depth knowledge of networking protocols and technologies, including TCP/IP, VLANs, OSPF, BGP, MPLS, VPNs, DNS, DHCP, SNMP, etc.
• Strong understanding of network security principles and best practices, including firewall configuration, intrusion detection/prevention, encryption, and secure remote access.
• Proficiency in network hardware and software, such as Arista, Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Aruba, etc. Experience with SDN, SD-WAN, and cloud networking is desirable.
• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex network issues.
• Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams, articulate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders, and mentor junior staff.
• Attention to detail, organization, and documentation skills, with a commitment to maintaining accurate network documentation and following standard procedures.
• Adaptability and willingness to learn new technologies, methodologies, and tools to keep pace with evolving business needs and industry trends.

This is an exciting opportunity to join us as an operations Instructor as part of the Nuclear Skills Alliance (NSA). • Communicate with external contractors if required to provide training support services
• Fully contribute to the business plan of the NSA to support achievement of our company organisational goals
Pay, benefits and culture

We are seeking an experienced Principal Flood Risk Consultant/Engineer who will play a leading role in the delivery of flood risk assessment and management solutions, hydraulic modelling and sustainable drainage projects for major development, regeneration and infrastructure schemes. Typically 7+ years' experience within flood risk, drainage or water consultancy.

Chartered or nearing Chartered status with CIWEM, ICE or a similar professional institution.

Strong understanding of UK flood risk policy, National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF), SuDS guidance and relevant industry standards.

Experience in producing and managing Flood Risk Assessments for planning and development projects.

Experience in developing and supervising surface water drainage strategies. Surface water drainage modelling (Microdrainage and Infodrainage). Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS) design and assessment.

Experience engaging with regulatory bodies including the Environment Agency, Lead Local Flood Authorities and water companies.
•
Understanding of catchment-based approaches and nature-based solutions to flood risk management would be advantageous.

Client-focused with a proactive and solution-oriented approach.

Previous experience in business development and client relationship management, with a keen interest in contributing to business growth.

Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs.

Passion for innovation, sustainability and climate resilience.

About the role:
This isn't just about designing processes; it's about owning the blueprint for our future. As the Operating Model Lead, you sit at the critical intersection of high-level strategy and real-world execution. You will translate ambitious strategic goals into a scalable, high-performance operational framework, ensuring that every transformation project we undertake is efficient, measurable, and deeply rooted in customer needs.
Design the Blueprint for How We Work
You are the architect of our transformation. Your primary mission is to lead the design of Target Operating Models (TOMs) for our most critical strategic programmes. You have the ultimate authority to sign off on the "operational architecture" before any detailed organizational design begins, ensuring our foundations are solid. By defining capabilities, integration points, and governance, you ensure our business evolves with purpose and precision.
Focus on the Customer Experience
We believe that great operational design starts with the customer. You will embed principles of ease, clarity, and responsiveness into every process and technology pillar you design. By mapping value streams and eliminating inefficiencies, you ensure that our internal workflows directly translate into exceptional, customer-centric experiences that differentiate us in the market.
Key Tasks/Areas of Responsibility
•
Transformation-Driven TOM Development: Lead the design of Target Operating Models (TOMs) for assigned strategic programmes and projects, defining the required operational architecture, key capabilities, and integration points necessary to deliver project outcomes and drive sustainable organisational transformation.
•
Customer-Centric Design Integration: Embed principles of great customer design—such as ease of navigation, clarity, and mobile responsiveness—into the Target Operating Model's process and technology pillars, ensuring all operational frameworks result in positive and effective customer experiences.
•
Process and Value Stream Mapping: Analyse current processes and value chains within the scope of the programme/project to identify inefficiencies. Design future-state business processes, standards, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to align with programme objectives.
•
Technology and Data Alignment: Partner with technology teams to define the required technical landscape, application architecture, and data governance needed to support the TOM within the scope of the programme/project.
•
Governance and Transformation Oversight: Define and establish the necessary governance framework, roles, and clear decision-making rights required for the successful operation of the programme's new model and its transition into the business, ensuring effective control over the transformation roadmap. Authority to sign off on the "operational architecture" before the Organisational Design Lead begins detailing "people structures"
•
Cross-Functional Blueprint: Create the programme-level operational blueprint and strategic blueprints that clearly outline the future structure of work, providing the necessary input for the Organisational Design function to define detailed people structures and roles.
•
Stakeholder Management: Secure project and programme stakeholder buy-in and maintain alignment across delivery workstreams by presenting model diagnostics, design options, and implementation readiness plans.
•
Industry Acumen: Maintain a deep understanding of industry trends, best practices, and emerging organisational models (e.g., agile, matrix structures).
•
Relationship Management: Foster strong working relationships with all levels of management, acting as a trusted advisor on operational effectiveness for strategic programmes.
•
Compliance and Policy Adherence: Ensure all model recommendations comply with legal, regulatory, and company policies.
•
Leadership Communication: Prepare and present formal recommendations, impact assessments, and reports on programme and project operating model designs to the Strategy and Transformation leadership.

- 7 years + minimum experience in a Transformation-Driven TOM Development Role

About This Job
This is a first-line product compliance role. You will work directly alongside engineers and product managers to translate regulatory obligations into product decisions that are scalable, defensible and globally consistent.
Your mission
Keeping pace with how money moves.  As Wise expands into new markets, corridors, and payment schemes, the rules governing how transfers are processed, and who can send them, become increasingly complex. You will own the compliance strategy for core product flows that determine customer eligibility: how we verify where customers live, how we handle customers who move between countries, and how we allocate customers to the right licensed entity. These aren't abstract compliance questions, they manifest directly in product screens, data models, and engineering decisions. You will need to go deep quickly, surface the "so what," and drive alignment between legal, product, and engineering teams across multiple markets.
Strengthening the infrastructure for regulatory accountability. Wise is continuously evolving the regulatory infrastructure that helps us demonstrate compliance across our licences, markets, and products. This platform connects our regulatory obligations to the policies, controls, … You'll help shape and strengthen this capability by partnering with engineers, product teams, and compliance specialists to ensure regulatory obligations are accurately reflected in our systems and translated into appropriate controls. You’ll also help make this scalable.
Staying ahead of global payment standards.  Wise operates across dozens of payment schemes and licensed entities worldwide. As international standards for payment messaging and data requirements evolve, you will own the compliance thread for how Wise's product and data infrastructure keeps pace, working closely with data engineering, scheme specialists, and regional legal counsel to ensure our payment flows are accurate, complete, and consistently applied across every market we operate in.
As Group Product Compliance Lead, you will:
•
Own compliance strategy and delivery across all of Wise for core domains such as payment processing, obligations to control mapping and verification standards
•
Translate complex, multi-jurisdictional obligations into actionable product and engineering decisions
•
Represent Wise's compliance position to regional regulators, internal forums, and external auditors where required
•
Build relationships with product, policy, and compliance teams globally to maintain a consistent and current view of obligations across markets
•
Help define and scale the assurance frameworks that give Wise confidence its controls are working
We are looking for someone who:
•
Has deep fintech compliance experience, with a track record of working directly in product teams, not alongside them
•
Is comfortable in codebases, engineering discussions, and architecture reviews; not intimidated by technical complexity
•
Can move between regulatory text and product specifications without losing either thread
•
Is a strong communicator who can synthesise regulatory complexity into a clear position for non-specialists
•
Is comfortable operating in ambiguity; capable of defining structure where none exists yet
•
Has a track record of influencing decisions across legal, engineering, and product at senior levels
•
Has familiarity with payment scheme rules (SEPA, SWIFT, domestic real-time rails)
•
Has experience with multi-entity or multi-licence compliance structures
•
Has working knowledge of KYC and identity verification frameworks and the product decisions that flow from them
In return, this role offers:
•
Real ownership: you ship things, you don't just advise
•
No regional or domain siloing; genuine cross-functional ownership spanning product, engineering, and compliance
•
The chance to shape infrastructure and frameworks that will operate at company scale, affecting every Wise customer and licensed entity
•
An exceptional cross-functional team across product, engineering, compliance, risk, and banking

Additional Information
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.
Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001495.description_excerpt:
About This Job
We're rebuilding how IFS ships software around autonomous, AI-native teams, and we're looking for someone to lead one. You'll write production code following agentic engineering principles, own it in production, and set the bar for a small team of engineers who do the same.
The software you'll build runs the real world. It's the workforce management & planning, project delivery and scheduling systems that construction and engineering companies use to run major programs. The people using it are planners, schedulers, project managers and site teams whose decisions carry real cost and real risk. When your code is right, their projects land. That's the feedback loop, and it's a good one.
What makes this different
We treat AI-assisted development as a core capability, not a novelty. Claude Code and Cursor are part of the daily workflow here, not something on a "tools we're evaluating" slide. We build agentic and LLM-backed features into the product, using RAG, agentic architectures, evaluation harnesses and context engineering, where they solve a real customer problem rather than chase a trend. If you've already changed how much you can ship and how fast because of the way you work with these tools, you'll be in good company.
We work in a forward-deployed way. You'll get into real customer environments, and shape the technical decisions, rather than working from a requirements document written by someone who's never been on site. Your goal will be to use these oppurtunities to bring customers the most value.
And you'll own the whole thing: design, build, test, deploy and run. Modern general-purpose languages, full stack, on a cloud-native platform with Kubernetes, CI/CD, IaC/GitOps and observability. Quality and security are built in as you go, not bolted on by a downstream gate.
What you'll do
Lead a small, autonomous team by setting technical direction, driving delivery and quality, and growing the engineers around you. Design and ship full-lifecycle features across front-end and back-end. Build and consume the APIs and event-driven services that connect workforce, project, scheduling and financial data across IFS Cloud and customer systems. Make performance and scalability decisions that hold under load. Get into customer environments, test your assumptions against reality, and bring that evidence back into the build. Document the why, not just the what, and help raise the practice of everyone you work alongside.

Qualifications
What we're looking for
A strong engineer who genuinely enjoys leading people and wants to stay close to the code while doing it. You take ownership without being asked, make progress when the brief is half-formed, and would rather ship and iterate than wait for perfect. You have depth in at least one area, whether that's front-end, back-end, data, quality, security, platform or applied AI, and the range to work across the stack. You've led or mentored engineers, and people tend to get better for having worked with you. You reason from the customer and commercial outcome as much as the technical one. And you're genuinely fluent with AI tools and agentic patterns in real engineering work, not just familiar with them.
Nice to have
A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field, or the equivalent proof in what you've built. Experience shipping AI-backed features such as LLM integration, RAG or agentic patterns. Experience with enterprise, ERP or project-based software, or exposure to construction, engineering or other field-heavy industries. Experience of agile delivery with globally distributed teams and leading them.

Additional Information
We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

Owns the front-end analysis that turns an emerging business need into a clearly defined, well-understood piece of work, with the outcome, scope, and rationale established before delivery begins.
Tech Solutions is MUFG Investor Services' technology organisation, reporting to the CTO. It's structured around five solution domains, each accountable for its own roadmap, budget, and outcomes. Within this structure, the role serves as a specialist analytical and subject-matter-expert resource aligned to the Fund Trading, BPO & Debt Services domain, while remaining deployable across domain boundaries as business priorities require.
The role brings deep investment-data and front-to-back operations expertise to the early stages of complex change — translating requirements into practical solution designs, and taking responsibility for the hands-on configuration of trade booking, pre-trade compliance, cash flow forecasting and liquidity, position-keeping, reconciliation, shadow NAV, and valuation. These capabilities underpin the service MUFG provides clients across front, middle, and back office, which is why the role is accountable for building and finalising that configuration itself, not just defining it.
Beyond the domain itself, the role contributes to the wider Tech Solutions organisation by building training material, artefacts, and knowledge-sharing forums — embedding this expertise more broadly and reducing dependency on any one person.

• Scientific domain knowledge in related fields such as environmental sciences or biology.
• Prior experience in developing machine-learning models relevant to biological or crop protection outcomes.

Job Description:
How do you design microwave electronics that still perform when speed, power and survivability really matter?
At Leonardo, our Electronic Warfare self‑protection systems are deployed across fast jet, UAV, land and naval platforms — operating in some of the most demanding RF environments in the world. As a Microwave Engineer or Senior Microwave Engineer, you’ll help develop and deliver the microwave subsystems that enable these platforms to detect, respond and survive. Based primarily at our Luton site, this role offers hybrid working, with on‑site time flexing to meet programme and test requirements.
What you’ll do
What you will do as a Microwave Engineer / Senior Microwave Engineer working on EW programmes:
• Develop microwave and RF circuits operating to and beyond 20 GHz, supporting advanced EW self‑protection systems.
• Contribute to the development of complex RF subsystems, from early prototyping through detailed design, integration and test.
• Perform microwave simulation, modelling and optimisation using industry‑standard EM and circuit tools.
• Perform hands‑on RF test, measurement and debug using world‑class laboratory facilities.
• Propose changes / updates as applicable.
• Contribute to and be supported by an Integrated Project Team.
• Engage in design reviews and technical discussions with internal stakeholders, partners and customers.
• In performing the above, solve technically challenging problems across the RF chain, balancing performance, power, reliability and manufacturability.
What you’ll bring
This role is aimed at engineers with microwave or RF expertise who are comfortable operating with some technical autonomy.
Essential experience:
• Proven experience working with RF / microwave circuitry in electronic systems.
• Understanding of microwave theory, high‑frequency effects and practical implementation including layout.
• Experience using one or more of:
• Keysight ADS
• Microwave Office
• CST Microwave Studio
• Ansys HFSS
• Siemens EDA / Mentor tools
• Hands‑on experience with RF test equipment, such as network analysers, spectrum analysers and RF sources.
• Ability to debug failing hardware or test setups.
• Practical experience analysing results and reporting against design requirements.
• Experience interfacing with customers, suppliers or internal stakeholders on technical matters.
• Teamworking: effective communication, undertaking activities in pursuit of the team’s goals and reporting on progress of these.
• Willingness to support and mentor less‑experienced early careers engineers.
Valuable (but not essential):
• Experience working within a structured electronic design lifecycle.
• Exposure to reporting on cost and schedule as well as technical progress.
• Experience within the defence or aerospace sector.
• Background in regulated or high‑reliability industries.
• HNC/HND or degree‑level knowledge in Electronic Engineering, Physics, Applied Physics or similar — or equivalent practical experience.
Experience in one or more of the following is advantageous:
• RF and microwave layout techniques
• RF synthesisers (DDS or PLL‑based)
• Mixers
• Frequency conversion
• Passive microwave structures (e.g. filters)
• High‑power amplifiers or switches
• Low phase‑noise design and measurement
• RF chain analysis and budgeting
• RF PCB design
• MMICs
• Antennas
• High speed digital circuitry
• Circuits operating across multi‑octave bandwidths
• Model‑driven engineering (MATLAB / Simulink)
• Test automation (e.g. LabVIEW)
How this role grows with you
This role rewards technical depth, judgement and delivery.
• Senior engineers operate with significant autonomy, owning complex microwave designs and solving demanding RF problems within EW systems.
• As influence and experience grow, progression to Principal Microwave Engineer brings broader technical authority — shaping subsystem architectures, guiding design standards and mentoring others.

Experience working in real estate or related industries is preferable but not essential.

Experience in gathering requirements and translating business needs into technical specifications.

Strong analytical skills, with the ability to collect, organise, analyse and share large amounts of information accurately and with attention to detail.

Adept at problem-solving, taking a broad perspective to identify or help define solutions

Locations: DD, PH, TD, IV, KY and DG
Are you a qualified Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer looking for excellent earning potential, structured work and the security of working directly for an established energy supplier?
At Utilita, we're growing our award-winning Field Services team. Join one of the UK's fastest-growing energy suppliers and a business that has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 Best Workplaces for four consecutive years.
What is in it for you?
You'll receive a base salary of £38,993, alongside uncapped earning potential and a variety of opportunities to boost your overall earnings, including:
• On-call payment: Receive £330 for each on-call week, based on an average rota of one week in five. (OTE of £42,293 just with the base salary and conducting mandatory on call requirements)
• Industry-leading installation bonus: Benefit from an uncapped installation bonus of £25 per meter or £50 per dual installation once you have completed a minimum of four installations in a day, with additional work opportunities available to further enhance your earnings.
• London weighting: Receive an additional £2,000 annual allowance if you live within the M25.
• Enhanced overtime: Enhanced overtime rates for Sunday working.
Alongside your salary and uncapped earning potential, you will receive 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, a healthcare scheme, mental wellbeing support, access to 24/7 GP and counselling services, and a generous pension scheme. You will also receive one paid volunteering day each year and have opportunities to win tickets to events at Utilita-sponsored arenas and football matches.
Why work at Utilita?
A schedule that supports your work-life balance.
We understand that a great Smart Meter Engineer role is not just about salary. It is also about having a structured working day and being able to plan your life accordingly.
You will be scheduled an average of 4 jobs per day, with an average travel time to jobs of approximately 35 minutes between appointments.
We aim to schedule your work several weeks in advance, giving you greater visibility of your schedule. This helps you plan life outside work while still giving you the opportunity to take on additional work when it suits you.
First-class training and support.
Your journey will begin at our award-winning training academy in Warrington, where you will receive a comprehensive induction.
You will then receive ongoing mentoring to help you strengthen your knowledge, understand our processes and confidently adapt to the Utilita way of working.
A team that keeps you connected.
We understand that working in the field can sometimes feel isolating, which is why creating a connected and supportive environment is so important to us.
Through regular manager check-ins, access to technical experts, collaborative colleague networks and ongoing communication, you'll always have the support you need and someone to turn to throughout your working day.
What you will be doing.
As a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer, you will represent Utilita in customers’ homes, installing smart meters safely and professionally across domestic properties.
You will play an important role in delivering our customer-first approach, providing a positive experience while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and service.
What we need from you.
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need:
• Smart Metering qualifications, including CCN1 or CMA1 and MET1, or equivalent.
• At least 12 months experience working as a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer.
• A valid full UK driving licence.
Who are Utilita?
Founded in 2003, Utilita Energy was created to challenge the Big Six energy suppliers by offering a fair and flexible service that is good for both the pocket and the planet.
As the first supplier to install a Smart Meter back in 2005 and kick-start Britain’s smart meter revolution, we continue to invest in smart technology and look for new ways to improve our services through innovation.
We are also committed to sustainability, with an ambition to become a Net Zero business by 2030. We believe everyone can make a meaningful impact through small, positive changes.
Our values are simple but powerful:
Fairness. Smart. Sustainability.
Our employees and customers come from all walks of life. We are committed to championing diversity, creating an inclusive culture and providing an environment where you can be your authentic self.
Utilita is part of the Luxion group which comprises Luxion Group Ltd, Utilita Energy Ltd, Luxion Sales Ltd, Utilita Field Services Ltd, Procode Technology Ltd and Canary Care Global Ltd.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.
